title: Metal composition of ambient PM2.5 influences severity of allergic airways disease in mice.
ehr_evidence: The study used no electronic health records; it collected ambient PM2.5 samples on Teflon filters in the cities of Zerbst and Hettstedt, eastern Germany (1999), and administered water/acid extracts to a well-characterized Balb/c mouse model of allergic airways disease induced by ovalbumin (OVA) antigen.
summary: In an experimental mouse model, intranasal administration of metal-rich ambient PM2.5 from the industrial city of Hettstedt (versus the cleaner city of Zerbst) enhanced allergic sensitization, airway hyperresponsiveness, and pulmonary inflammation following ovalbumin challenge.
key_findings: Hettstedt PM2.5 administered 2 hr before OVA challenge increased PenH (airway responsiveness) by 190% versus baseline in allergic mice (p<0.05), whereas Zerbst PM2.5 and control filter extract increased PenH by 120% and 44%, respectively.

Hettstedt PM2.5 before challenge significantly increased methacholine responsiveness and BAL eosinophil numbers (3-fold) versus Zerbst PM2.5, control extract, and nonallergic Hettstedt-exposed mice (p<0.05).
Hettstedt PM2.5 increased serum OVA-specific IgE whether administered before sensitization or before challenge (p<0.05).
Both Hettstedt and Zerbst PM2.5 significantly increased BAL protein, LDH, and NAG (lung injury) and raised proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IFN-γ by 6- to 8-fold versus control extract (p<0.05).
Hettstedt PM2.5 significantly increased BAL protein (256 ± 32 vs 177 ± 7 µg/mL) and NAG (2.9 ± 0.5 vs 1.6 ± 0.2 U/L) versus control in nonallergic mice (p<0.05).
Lead and copper were ~7-fold greater, cadmium ~5-fold greater, and tin and arsenic ~4-fold and ~3-fold greater in Hettstedt PM2.5 than Zerbst PM2.5.

No significant differences in BAL inflammatory cells or airway responses were observed when PM2.5 was administered before sensitization (except IgE), and most effects were transient, diminishing by 7 days after challenge.
captured_features: PM2.5 elemental composition (26 elements by ICP-MS; sulfate by ICP-AES)
PenH (enhanced pause) and PenH AUC (methacholine responsiveness)
BAL cell differentials (eosinophils, neutrophils, macrophages, lymphocytes)
BAL cytokines (IL-1β, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-13, MIP-2, TNF-α, IFN-γ)
study_design: Experimental animal study (mouse model of allergic airways disease)
population: Young adult female Balb/c mice (7 weeks old, 18-21 g) exposed to ovalbumin
exposure_domain: Air pollution (ambient PM2.5) and heavy metals
limitations: Small group sizes in some time points (e.g., n=2-3 at 7 days), so 7-day responses were not statistically analyzed.
Observed effects were transient, diminishing to control levels by 7 days after challenge.
Only two cities compared, limiting generalizability of PM2.5 composition effects.
Mouse model may not fully replicate human allergic airway disease.
Endotoxin levels were very low in both samples, so endotoxin was not responsible for the observed effects.
